opportunities.title: Service-line front door: qualified intake, inspection request booking and a machine-readable listing
opportunities.problem: Seven very different service lines (geotechnical, environmental/LSRP, vibration monitoring, hazmat/mold, noise/air, special inspection, site civil) all land in the same six-field contact form, so a hazmat survey request and a special-inspection request arrive in one undifferentiated queue. There is no quote calculator, no booking link and no client portal, the contact page omits the street address and map, and the form combines reCAPTCHA with a honeypot field that can silently discard autofilled or agent-submitted enquiries. The public listing compounds this: 2.1 stars, no photos, and Friday hours that disagree with the firm's own job postings.
evidence: Seven practice pages listed on the Services page, all funnelling to one generic contact form with fixed fields (name, email, phone, company, city, message) and no service selector: https://distinct-esi.com/services/

Form is a WordPress Forminator form protected by reCAPTCHA and a hidden honeypot labelled 'Please do not fill in this field.', which can silently drop automated or autofilled submissions: https://distinct-esi.com/contact/

No online booking, quote flow or portal link anywhere in navigation; the home page's only conversion CTAs are 'OUR SERVICES' and 'CONTACT US'; no JSON-LD structured data and an empty meta description: https://distinct-esi.com/

Google Business Profile shows 2.1 stars, category 'Engineering consultant', no photos, and Friday hours 9 AM-6 PM versus 9 AM-5 PM in job postings: https://www.google.com/maps/place/Distinct+Engineering+Solutions,+Inc./@40.4346013,-74.4850476,17z
Contact page publishes four tel: links and two generic inboxes but no street address or embedded map: https://distinct-esi.com/contact/
opportunities.agent_design: Replace the single form with a service-line intake agent that asks 4-6 scope questions per line (for special inspection: borough, DOB job number, phase and trade; for hazmat: building type, age and whether an ACM/lead survey is required; for geotech: site address, proposed structure and boring availability), classifies the request, checks it against the firm's service area and prequalifications, drafts an acknowledgement listing the documents needed, and offers a booked call or site-visit slot on the responsible project manager's calendar. It writes a structured record (service line, site, client type, urgency, owner) to a lightweight CRM or spreadsheet and posts to the right inbox, so nothing waits in a shared queue. Human approval sits on any priced quote, any out-of-scope or out-of-area request, and any emergency/after-hours dispatch. In parallel the same work package publishes ProfessionalService/LocalBusiness JSON-LD, real meta descriptions per service page, a consistent hours/address record, and a post-project review-request sequence that a partner approves before send.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A form plugin cannot ask different scoping questions per service line, classify free-text into the right PM, check certifications and service area, or write a routed record into a calendar and CRM; and the current honeypot/reCAPTCHA combination actively breaks unattended submissions. The difference between a form and a front door is the routing logic, the document checklist and the approval gates, not the text box.

impact_estimate.range: $3,000-$6,000/yr of recovered admin and triage time, plus recovery of enquiries currently at risk of silent drop (volume unquantified, so no revenue is claimed).
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 2-4 inbound enquiries per week that currently need 3-4 email round-trips to qualify (about 2-4 hrs/week), paid at the NJ median customer-service wage of $47,740 (2025) plus roughly 30% loaded overhead; the honeypot and missing service selector are treated as lost-enquiry risk only, because DESI publishes no inbound volume or conversion data. Schema, meta and Google-profile fixes are credited as credibility and AI-discoverability hygiene, not revenue.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Three weeks: live intake agents for the three highest-value lines (special inspection, hazmat, geotechnical), a bookable 20-minute scoping call, structured enquiry dashboard by service line, plus JSON-LD, meta descriptions, corrected hours/address and a photo-and-review plan for the Google profile. Success measured as time-to-first-response and the share of enquiries that arrive with the documents needed.

opportunities.title: Field inspection scheduling, dispatch and report-chasing agent
opportunities.problem: DESI is hiring a full-time Scheduling Coordinator to coordinate inspectors' daily schedules, talk to clients and project managers, and track and review inspection reports - a dispatch-and-chase role created because field volume is growing. The firm is simultaneously planning 14+ hires including four NICET II/III construction inspectors, and its field staff work across NYC and NJ job sites (bridges, tunnels, LIRR track, NYCHA housing, bulkheads). With no client portal and no published on-call route despite a '24/7, if needed' service claim, scheduling and report status live in email and phone calls.
evidence: Scheduling Coordinator posting (full-time, on-site, North Brunswick) covers inspectors' daily schedules, client and PM communication, and tracking/reviewing inspection reports: https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/scheduling-coordinator-at-distinct-engineering-solutions-inc-4465325907

Careers page plans 8 entry-level engineers/scientists/inspectors plus 4 NICET II/III construction inspectors, attributing hiring to increased workload and backlog from existing contracts: https://distinct-esi.com/careers/

Corporate summary distinguishes office professional staff from 'field personnel', consistent with inspectors deployed to job sites rather than a fixed desk: https://distinct-esi.com/corporate-summary/
Clients page states services are provided '24/7, if needed' with no published on-call number or escalation route: https://distinct-esi.com/clients/
Careers page also plans 2 experienced geotechnical/environmental engineers and cites 'many new opportunities', i.e. more concurrent jobs to schedule: https://distinct-esi.com/careers/
opportunities.agent_design: An event-driven scheduling agent takes inspection requests from the intake agent, agency portals and email, and builds a daily deployment plan: it matches each job's required certification (NICET II/III, NYC DOB Class I Special Inspection Agency scope, AASHTO lab test type) against inspector credentials, clusters visits by borough/site, drafts client and inspector confirmations, and flags conflicts, travel gaps and uncovered jobs. A second loop watches report due dates against actual submissions, chases missing field data and photos from inspectors, and escalates slipping reports to the Scheduling Coordinator and PM with the client's deadline attached. It reads and writes calendar and email and can sit in front of a spreadsheet or LIMS export; nothing is ripped out. Human approval is required for any schedule change after confirmation, overtime or after-hours dispatch, reassignment between inspectors, and any client-facing commitment on report timing. The on-call claim gets a published escalation route with a human always answering the escalation.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This needs a credentials matrix (which inspector may sign which inspection in which jurisdiction), calendar and email integration, deadline state that persists across days, and an audit trail a public-agency client can inspect. A chatbot cannot hold multi-week report state or enforce certification rules; a generic scheduling app cannot reason over free-text job scopes and inspection reports.

impact_estimate.range: $8,000-$20,000/yr of coordinator time, plus faster report-to-invoice turnaround.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference from the posting that a coordinator's day is roughly half scheduling and half report chasing; assumes 25-40% of that is automatable (1-1.6 hrs/day over ~250 working days) at the NJ median customer-service wage of $47,740 plus ~30% loaded overhead, with the top of the range including after-hours routing and fewer missed or re-booked inspections. Field-service routing case studies report large dispatcher-time reductions (one vendor case study cites 3 hours to 45 minutes per day) but are customer-reported software results, not AI trials, so they are used only to sanity-check direction. Faster report submission shortening the invoice cycle is an inference, not a measured saving.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Four weeks on one line (special inspection / construction administration): build the inspector certification matrix, generate a daily draft schedule with confirmations, run a report-status board with automatic chasers and escalations, and publish an on-call escalation route. Measured as coordinator hours per week, on-time report rate and re-booked visits.

opportunities.title: Bid discovery and proposal-compliance agent for multi-state public work
opportunities.problem: DESI has just created a full-time Proposal Coordinator role whose work is reading RFP/RFQ requirements, tracking deadlines, collecting inputs from engineering, operations and finance, maintaining a proposal content library, and submitting packages through client portals or email. Behind that role sits a wide prequalification footprint (NJ DPMC, PANYNJ, NYC SCA, DASNY, NJ Turnpike, PennDOT ECMS, plus DBE/MBE in four states), which means monitoring many agency portals at once, and a careers page that attributes hiring to backlog and 'many new opportunities'. A single missed addendum or compliance item can disqualify a sealed public submission.
evidence: Proposal Coordinator posting (0-3 years, full-time, on-site) covers RFP/RFQ requirement review, deadline tracking, coordinating inputs from engineering/operations/finance, maintaining a proposal content library, and submitting via online portals or email: https://www.mediabistro.com/jobs/3542836748-proposal-coordinator

Qualifications page lists NJ/NY/CT/PA DBE and MBE, PANYNJ MBE/DBE, NYC DOB Class I Special Inspection Agency, A2LA ISO/IEC 17020 (cert. 4048.01) and AASHTO lab accreditation - a document-heavy library that proposals must cite accurately: https://distinct-esi.com/qualifications/
Careers page attributes 14+ planned hires to backlog from existing contracts and 'many new opportunities': https://distinct-esi.com/careers/

ACEC Research Institute (May 2025): marketing and sales is the highest AI-use area at 81% of firms, 'AI-assisted proposal writing' is a named common use case, and 68% of firms believe they can automate 10-29% of current work tasks; 74% expect to maintain staffing while increasing output (association survey of self-reported expectations, not measured savings): https://www.acec.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/The-Role-of-Artificial-Intelligence-in-the-Engineering-Industry.pdf

Blog project notes show active multi-site work (LIRR Expansion, NYCHA Sandy rehabilitation, a Morris County bridge replacement, bulkhead rehabilitation) that proposal teams must mine for project sheets: https://distinct-esi.com/blog/
opportunities.agent_design: A discovery loop checks the agency portals DESI is prequalified on plus email bid notifications daily, matches each notice to the firm's service lines, prequalification codes and geography, and posts a short go/no-go brief with scope, due date, bonding/insurance requirements and the named decision-maker. On a go, a proposal agent builds a compliance matrix from the RFP (every requirement mapped to a response owner), a deadline and addendum calendar that alerts on portal Q&A changes, and a first draft of the non-technical sections (firm background, certifications, safety, resumes, project sheets) pulled from a structured content library. It tracks which engineer owes which section and chases them. Human approval is mandatory on the go/no-go call, every technical section, pricing, and the final package: a person reviews, seals and submits through the portal; the agent never submits a bid or signs anything.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The value is in the state machine around a bid - which portal, which addendum superseded which page, which certification expires before the submission date, which engineer still owes a section - plus retrieval over the firm's own project sheets and resumes. Off-the-shelf chat assistants cannot poll portals, diff addenda, enforce a compliance matrix or keep an auditable library, and feeding unpublished bid documents and private client details into a consumer tool is an NDA and confidentiality problem.

impact_estimate.range: $15,000-$45,000/yr of proposal labour, on an assumed 30-50 submissions a year.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Submission volume is not published; 30-50 responses a year is an inference from the newly created full-time proposal role, the multi-state prequalification list and the stated backlog. Assumes a 20-40% reduction in labour per response limited to drafting, compliance tracking and library assembly (the Science 2023 experiment measured a 40% time reduction on 20-30 minute professional writing tasks, and ACEC reports 68% of firms expecting 10-29% of tasks automatable), plus 10-20 engineer hours saved per response at the NJ median civil-engineer wage of $104,660 plus ~30% overhead. Technical judgement, PE review and sealing are excluded from the saving, and no new-win revenue is claimed.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Four weeks: monitor three portals (e.g. PANYNJ, NYC SCA/PASSPort, NJ DPMC) with a daily matched-bid digest, then run one live proposal end to end - compliance matrix, addendum tracking, structured content library seeded from existing project sheets and certifications, and drafted non-technical sections for the proposal lead to review and submit.

lead_score.rationale: Pain evidence is strong and specific: three back-office roles posted in parallel (Scheduling Coordinator, Proposal Coordinator, Project Controller) each describe manual coordination work, the careers page puts hiring down to backlog plus 'many new opportunities', and the front door really is one generic form with a silent-drop honeypot, no booking and a 2.1-star listing with no photos. Fit is high because intake (G), field dispatch and report chasing (A) and bid/proposal discovery (B) map almost one-to-one onto the firm's own job descriptions, so the pilot can be judged against a role DESI is already paying for. Ability to pay is scored 14/20: 30+ staff, four-state DBE/MBE prequalifications, an AASHTO-accredited lab and public-agency clients imply real budget, but revenue is unpublished, public-sector fees are competitively bid, and a 30-person firm will buy in small phases. Ease is 11/15 - the front-door and proposal pilots need little more than email, calendar and portal access, while dispatch needs a credential matrix and integrations. Strategic value is 13/15 because service-line intake, inspector dispatch and RFP compliance recur in every civil/geotechnical/environmental consultancy, making this a repeatable vertical play. Ordering: front door (G) first as a low-cost credibility and routing fix, then proposals (B) because the pain is already funded by a new hire, then dispatch (A) as the larger integration. Capability E was considered and deliberately not proposed: no avenues.json was supplied in this folder, so there is no verified design, model set, legal note or pilot shape to build on, and the observable evidence points at scheduling and paperwork rather than at lab or site-sensor bottlenecks. The AASHTO soil/concrete lab and the field inspection work are plausible E territory (cylinder counting and labelling, curing-room temperature, equipment utilisation), but confirming it needs a site visit rather than a web inference, so it is queued as a walk-in discovery item rather than scored as an opportunity. No security, intrusion or surveillance use case is proposed; any later security-adjacent camera work would be installed by a licensed NJ alarm or electrical contractor under N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2 as amended by P.L.2021, c.2.

best_evidence_signal: Three newly created back-office roles posted in parallel - Scheduling Coordinator, Proposal Coordinator and Project Controller - each describing manual coordination, chasing and submission work an agent could absorb: https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/scheduling-coordinator-at-distinct-engineering-solutions-inc-4465325907
